title: plugin-view ObjectView: handleRefresh is declared and never referenced — a dead refresh entry point
body:
Observation-class finding, measured while tracing the refresh signal for #4549. Nothing a user hits today — filing so it is not re-discovered.

## What was measured

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:608` declares:

```ts
const handleRefresh = useCallback(() => {
  setRefreshKey(prev => prev + 1);
}, []);
```

Grepping the package for the identifier returns the declaration and nothing else:

```
$ grep -rn "handleRefresh" packages/plugin-view/src/
packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:608:  const handleRefresh = useCallback(() => {
```

It is not passed to the toolbar, not exposed on a handle, not wired to any control. Of the component's six `setRefreshKey` sites it is the only one with no caller.

For contrast, the other five are all reachable in at least one mount: the `onMutation` auto-subscribe (guarded off when `renderListView` is supplied), `handleDelete` / `handleBulkDelete` (wired to the built-in ObjectGrid branch), and `handleFormSuccess` (wired to the form's `onSuccess`).

## Why it is worth a line

It reads as "ObjectView has a refresh entry point" to anyone scanning for one — which is exactly the question #4549 had to answer, and the dead declaration cost a detour to rule out. Either wire it to a real affordance (a toolbar refresh button) or delete it; the current state advertises a capability that does not exist.

Refs #4549.
